288: At tree level, the spectral action Tr f(D_K^2/Lambda^2) generates the Einstein-Hilbert action through the a_2 term (Paper 06, eq. 3.20). The Einstein equations are then variational consequences of the spectral action. The EIH self-energy is a post-Newtonian consequence of these Einstein equations. So the chain:
  289: 
  290:     D_K -> S[D_K] = Tr f(D_K^2/Lambda^2) -> G_eff from a_2 -> EIH corrections -> delta_D_G -> D_K + delta_D_G
  291: 
  292: is entirely internal to the spectral action framework. Each step follows from the previous one. The loop closes at O(alpha_G). The fixed point of this loop (if one iterates) converges rapidly because alpha_G = 9.3 x 10^{-4} << 1: the correction to the correction is O(alpha_G^2) ~ 10^{-6}.
  293: 
  294: However, the NON-PERTURBATIVE closure is a different matter. The spectral action Tr f(D^2/Lambda^2) is defined for a FIXED Dirac operator D. The bootstrap loop asks: what is the self-consistent D such that the gravitational field it generates, acting back on itself, reproduces D? This is a self-consistency equation:

  296:     D_K = D_K^{bare} + delta_D_G[a_2(D_K)]
  297: 
  298: This is a fixed-point equation on the space of Dirac operators. In the NCG literature, there is no general existence or uniqueness theorem for such self-consistent spectral triples. The closest result is the inner fluctuation formalism (Connes-Chamseddine, Paper 06 Section 4.4), where inner automorphisms A -> A + Juge A Juge^{-1} + a[D,b] gen
